name: Global Static Indexing for Regular Grids
definition: A storage layout and indexing scheme for rectilinear grids that minimizes disk I/O during progressive traversal by reordering data based on a 2^n tree decomposition (Lebesgue curve) instead of a binary tree, enabling out-of-core visualization of very large grids (e.g., 8192^3) with modest memory (60MB).
summary: Global Static Indexing is a storage layout for rectilinear grids that minimizes disk I/O by reordering data via 2^n tree decomposition, enabling fast out-of-core visualization with modest memory.
